classes.name: bond equivalent yield
classes.label: bond equivalent yield
classes.definition: Yield determined on an equivalent basis to the yield of another bond. This is used to be able to realistically compare prices between debt instruments across different markets.

classes.name: credit spread
classes.label: credit spread
classes.definition: yield spread that reflects the additional net yield an investor can earn from a security with more credit risk relative to one with less credit risk

classes.name: current yield calculation method
classes.label: current yield calculation method
classes.definition: The ratio of the interest payment amount to the clean price.

classes.name: debt convexity analytic
classes.label: debt convexity analytic
classes.definition: The second derivative of a security's price with respect to its yield, divided by the security's price. A security exhibits positive convexity when its price rises more for a downward move in its yield than its price declines for an equal upward move in its yield. Further notes: A measure of the change in price for a given change in Modified Duration. This always (necessarily) refers to Modified Duration. This is used as another risk measurement. Numerator is always (a) duration - either MacCaulays or Modified. Always rate of change of (one of the) Duration against some other parameter. The other paramater can be characterised as a Yield (it may be the Price, but that has a relationship to the Yield in any case). REVIEW: Inconsistency in the above - is it always necessarily Modified Duration that is referred to, or "any" Duration measure (Macaulays and.or Modified)? notes 9 Dec A measure of the sensitivity of the price with reference to interest rates. This is normally determined with reference to maturity, but since there are different maturity dates, this figure gives an estimate of the equitvalent if you had a homogenous portfolio, i.e. this is an estimate based on a pure equivalent, homogenous portfolio. Convexity of instrument versus portfolio. Sees instrument in terms of the set of cashflows. The term Convexity can be applied either to a bond or to a portfolio. More notes: When you get Convexit in MD, it will tell you what Duration it is refrfering to, along with Redemption Date (logically). Also if there is Option Adjusted Yield, there is a third set of analytics. What are they? i.e. OA Convexity, Duration Yield and the rest. Conclusions: Agreed to revisit this in OTC.

classes.name: debt instrument yield
classes.label: debt instrument yield
classes.definition: The return on the debt instrument at the stated price.

classes.name: debt price spread
classes.label: debt price spread

classes.name: debt securities market maker

classes.name: debt yield to average life
classes.label: debt yield to average life
classes.definition: The yield achieved by substituting a bond's average life for the issue's final maturity date.

classes.name: debt yield to equivalent life
classes.label: debt yield to equivalent life
classes.definition: The yield achieved by substituting a bond's equivalent life for the issue's final maturity date.

classes.name: debt yield to maturity
classes.label: debt yield to maturity
classes.definition: The internal rate of return an investor would achieve if he or she purchased that bond at its current dirty price, and held it to maturity, assuming all coupon and principal payments are received as scheduled.

classes.name: debt yield to next call
classes.label: debt yield to next call
classes.definition: The yield of a bond to the next possible call date.

classes.name: debt yield to worst
classes.label: debt yield to worst
classes.definition: Yield to the worst case of when the instrument might be called.

classes.name: discounted instrument yield
classes.label: discounted instrument yield
classes.definition: Yield quoted for a discount instrument. This is the ratio of the discount to the face value, divided by the period to maturity as a fraction of a year.

classes.name: duration analytic
classes.label: duration analytic

classes.name: f f i e c up 300 prepay speed

classes.name: i c m a yield formula
classes.label: i c m a yield formula
classes.definition: The calculation method specified by ICMA (formerly ISMA) for determination of yield for fixed-rate bonds.

classes.name: internally determined price spread
classes.label: internally determined price spread
classes.definition: The spread determined internally within the organisation from information available at their own trading desks. Further Notes Internal prices within a bank would be determined by surveying their own traders. So e.g. corporate desk trades these 30 bonds, get the daily spreads on those at the end of the day and calculate the price. The traders determine the pricing during the based on market movements. (this is all for OTC traded bonds, not exchange traded bonds).

classes.name: life analytic
classes.label: life analytic
classes.definition: Some measure of the life of a security, other than the actual time to maturity itself. This is a derived figure, based on certain parameters as appropriate to that type of instrument, to give a figure that is equivalent to and similar to the basic maturity of the instrument, for the purposes of analysing that security.

classes.name: loan pool prepayment model
classes.label: loan pool prepayment model
classes.definition: Model of the prepayments of loans in a pool of individual loans, such as a mortgage pool or loan pool.

classes.name: loan prepayment formula
classes.label: loan prepayment formula
classes.definition: The formula which embodies the model for loan pool prepayment speed.

classes.name: maturity equivalent p s a
classes.label: maturity equivalent p s a
classes.definition: Prepayment speed that results in the same average life as that computed for the Collateralized Mortgage Obligation (CMO), Asset Backed Securities (ABS) or Mortgage Backed Securities (MBS) using the Maturity Prepay Model.

classes.name: modified duration analytic
classes.label: modified duration analytic
classes.definition: The percentage price change of a security for a given change in yield. The higher the modified duration of a security, the higher its risk. Ad/ModDuration = [duration / {1 + (IRR/M)}]; where IRR is the internal rate of return and M is the number of compounding periods per year.

classes.name: native yield
classes.label: native yield
classes.definition: The yield of the security as determined using the Yield Calculation Method that is the default for the market that the security is traded in.

classes.name: native yield calculation method
classes.label: native yield calculation method

classes.name: next call
classes.label: next call
classes.definition: The next call of the issue, as at the current time.

classes.name: next call date
classes.label: next call date
classes.definition: The next date on which the issue can be called, from the present date.

classes.name: next put
classes.label: next put
classes.definition: The next available put date for the issue, as at the current time.

classes.name: o t c bond market price
classes.label: o t c bond market price
classes.definition: The price determined for the marketplace for a bond which is traded over the counter.

classes.name: option adjusted yield
classes.label: option adjusted yield
classes.definition: NB specified as a spread. synonym: OAS Based on different Int Rate paths. There are different OAS models just like there are different Yield methods. Also would make reference to the Yield Curve - but these are parameters that go into that model. Limit this model at the point where it distinguishes the difference between things - we are not in a position to mathematically model the things themselves, just capture the basic facts.

classes.name: partial calls estimation model
classes.label: partial calls estimation model
classes.definition: A model of how the early partial calls are estimated.

classes.name: pool factor
classes.label: pool factor
classes.definition: How much of the original pool is still outstanding. This is a number below one. Expressed as percentage.

classes.name: pool paydown rate
classes.label: pool paydown rate
classes.definition: The rate at which the pool is paying down. This is based on observed factor. CPR, SMM, etc. etc. Measured differently for different kinds of security. CBO might have a prepayment rate for example if the underlying bond is callable. with a non agency mortgge dela, defualts will effect this. so for instance there is principal is no lnger inthe pool because the mortgagee defaults. With agency these are not taken out in the case of default but for non agency these mortgages are removed from the pool if and when a mortgagee defualts.

classes.name: price value of basis point
classes.label: price value of basis point
classes.definition: Sensitivity of the price for one basis point change in yield, defined as the difference in price given 1 bp change in yield.

classes.name: russian yield calculation method
classes.label: russian yield calculation method
classes.definition: The method used in determining Yield in the Russian markets. This is based on an effective yield with fundamentally different math. To give an example of the use of a different "yield type", we have Russia, which trades based on an effective yield. The price-yield math is fundamentally different. Notes Origin:Fidessa Uses a trade space and effective yield formula. MAy have same day types but different math.

classes.name: simple yield calculation method

attributes.name: price quoted ex dividend
attributes.label: price quoted ex dividend
attributes.definition: Whether or not the yield is based on a price which is quoted ex-dividend. When a bond is said to trade ex-dividend it means that there is a period of time prior to each coupon payment during which a bond purchaser does not receive custody of the next coupon. That payment is made to the previous bond holder and accrued interest is therefore negative during the ex-dividend period.
